messages:
dana: Heads-up — noticed a regression on dedicated INT8 pool after yesterday's kernel-selector change. KV cache memory climbs steadily on long contexts (>6k tokens) and we see a lot more small live slots instead of coalesced ranges. Repro: session stream with multi-turn doc ingestion.
priya: ugh, saw this morning too. telemetry shows slot count doubles over ~200s for one user thread. CPU stays stable, GPU mem increases ~350MB.
matt: any chance the kernel fallback that we added for INT8 microkernels affects cache write ordering? that could fragment slab allocations.
koen: profiling suggests two differences: (1) blocking kernel path increases per-token tail latency which extends kv residency; (2) the INT8 packing introduced 8-byte alignment padding in the slot header. small slots + padding -> holes.
jules: reproducer? can you paste the minimal harness/query and perf traces?
dana: minimal run (single client):
```
# run with long context + repeated prefixes
./run_infer --model=mosaic-int8 --ctx=8192 --prompt-file=long_doc.txt --stream
```
Attached heap-snapshots from allocator: incremental slot growth with many 64-256B entries.
priya: i ran a memory flame query, results:
```
SELECT slot_size, count(*) FROM kv_slots WHERE session_id='repro-2299' GROUP BY slot_size ORDER BY slot_size;
# -> buckets: 64: 1200, 128: 950, 256: 340, 512+: 80
```
koen: that distribution screams fragmentation. two immediate ideas: compact-on-evict and proactive coalesce after quantize pass. compacting on the hot path is risky for latency.
matt: agree. maybe we can piggyback compaction during idle scheduling windows (background thread) and add a heuristics gate: only coalesce slots if free_mem < threshold and fragmentation_metric > X.
dana: what about the accuracy angle? ops worried INT8 quantization + compaction/slot-migration might reorder KV addresses and change alignment-dependent kernel fast paths. did we see fidelity drift?
jules: small check — eval harness against our regression prompt-set shows a tiny drop in recall @k after the kernel-selector change: 0.6% absolute on a few Llama-variant prompts when using INT8 + long context. BF16 baseline unaffected.
priya: drilled into logits diffs; most deltas are near-zero but a few amplify after slot warmup events (when eviction/prefetch kicks in). hypothesis: when slots are reinserted they land at different physical page & cache line offsets which affects fused attention kernel quant accumulation path numerics slightly.
koen: sounds like micro-architectural nondeterminism + quantization error. mitigation options: (A) add deterministic slot placement (align to 4K boundaries) to avoid partial-cacheline overlap for KV pairs, (B) increase INT8 dequant compensation term in kernels, (C) prefer BF16 for sessions > X tokens.
matt: (A) increases external fragmentation, but might lower numeric variance. worth testing. (B) requires kernel change and perf run. (C) easy product fallback policy: route longctx sessions to BF16 unless customer explicitly pins INT8. fallback could be automated only when we detect rising fragmentation.
dana: operationally we need a short-term fix (low-risk) + a medium-term kernel fix. short-term: enable background compaction with conservative thresholds + revert kernel-selector change for INT8 until we validate.
perf-bot: ALERT: capacity-regression detected on int8-pool-3 at 2299012370 (observed GPU mem growth >300MB/session compared to baseline). Ticket created: PERF-8421.
jules: ok i can revert selector on canaries for the next deploy window. priya — can you run an A/B with background compaction enabled on canary for 2h and collect eval diffs?
priya: will run now. quick questions for metrics: collect slot_count, fragmentation_ratio (free_slots.size / total_slots), mean_slot_age, and eval recall/delta. anything else?
koen: add kernel-path-counters: fast_int8_hits, fallback_int8_hits, bf16_hits. also trace kernel latency p50/p95 for the two paths.
dana: also capture page-mapping histograms (pages moved per minute) and GC pause histograms.
matt: we should add a micro-benchmark that explicitly forces partial-page slots to see numeric divergence, to isolate whether dequant/accum is the culprit.
jules: sgtm. let's coordinate: priya run canary A/B, matt & koen prep micro-bench and kernel patch plan, i'll revert selector on canary. dana will monitor perf-bot and draft customer note if needed.
priya: A/B started (canary nodes: int8-pool-3a). collecting evals and telemetry; ETA 2h.
dana: thanks. please post results here. if the regression persists after compaction we escalate kernel changes. :thumbsup:
